referenced_urls.title: The Inbox as a Coordination Primitive for LLM Agent Societies

relevance: Asynchronous inboxes as a building block for multi-agent systems.

media.description: Abstract excerpt of 'The Inbox as a Coordination Primitive': pull-based inboxes with private reading rules, studied in simulated societies of up to 16,000 LLM agents.
media.ocr_text: Language-model agents increasingly coordinate in large groups, and current agent protocols focus on delivering messages. For these agents, however, the scarce resource is not delivery but reading: every message costs tokens, and the context is finite. Current infrastructure works by push: the sender decides when a message enters the recipient's context, so the recipient reads in arrival order and drops the oldest messages once its context is full. We study the alternative, pull, in which messages wait in an inbox outside the context and the recipient's own rules decide what it reads and keeps. We argue that the inbox is a coordination primitive: each agent sets its rules privately, and those rules decide whether other agents' requests reach it.
